findings.title: Default proto codec rejects APIv1-only (legacy) messages
findings.why_it_matters: Every RPC that uses a message type generated by pre-1.4 protoc-gen-go (or any other APIv1-only implementation without a ProtoReflect method) now fails in both directions with "failed to marshal, message is %T, want proto.Message". This is the default codec for all gRPC calls. Before this change, the codec imported github.com/golang/protobuf/proto, whose Message is protoiface.MessageV1 (Reset/String/ProtoMessage) and which converted to v2 internally. Now it imports google.golang.org/protobuf/proto, whose Message is protoreflect.ProtoMessage and requires ProtoReflect(). That breaks the stated constraint that callers passing APIv1 messages must keep working. Accepting both shapes and converting with protoadapt.MessageV2Of restores the old contract without going back to the deprecated module.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a helper `func messageV2Of(v any) proto.Message { switch v := v.(type) { case protoadapt.MessageV1: return protoadapt.MessageV2Of(v); case protoadapt.MessageV2: return v }; return nil }` and use `vv := messageV2Of(v); if vv == nil { return ..., fmt.Errorf(...) }` in both Marshal and Unmarshal. Add a codec test using a hand-written legacy struct that implements only Reset/String/ProtoMessage and carries protobuf struct tags.
evidence: encoding/proto/proto.go:41 -- vv, ok := v.(proto.Message)   (proto is now google.golang.org/protobuf/proto, i.e. protoreflect.ProtoMessage requiring ProtoReflect())
encoding/proto/proto.go:49 -- vv, ok := v.(proto.Message)   (same check in Unmarshal)

diff: -	"github.com/golang/protobuf/proto" +	"google.golang.org/protobuf/proto" in encoding/proto/proto.go imports; github.com/golang/protobuf@v1.5.3 proto.Message = protoiface.MessageV1 (Reset/String/ProtoMessage only)
provenance: da3facf0 move from github.com/golang/protobuf to google.golang.org/protobuf/proto (introduced on this branch)

findings.title: Status.Details returns wrapper type for legacy APIv1 details
findings.why_it_matters: If a status detail's registered type is an APIv1-only (legacy) message, status.Details() now returns an internal *impl.messageIfaceWrapper instead of the caller's concrete type. Callers that type-assert details (for example `d.(*mypb.ErrorInfo)`) then silently stop matching. Before this change, ptypes.UnmarshalAny with DynamicAny went through ptypes.Empty, which returned proto.MessageV1(mt.New().Interface()) and so unwrapped legacy messages back to their original Go type. any.UnmarshalNew() returns the raw v2 Interface(), which for legacy types is the wrapper. WithDetails was deliberately widened to accept protoadapt.MessageV1, so the read path should give back the same v1 shape symmetrically.
findings.suggested_fix: Change line 163 to `details = append(details, protoadapt.MessageV1Of(detail))`, which matches the old ptypes.Empty behavior (proto.MessageV1 == protoimpl.X.ProtoMessageV1Of). Add a status test that round-trips a legacy APIv1 detail through WithDetails/Details and type-asserts the result.
evidence: internal/status/status.go:158-163 -- detail, err := any.UnmarshalNew() ... details = append(details, detail)
github.com/golang/protobuf@v1.5.3/ptypes/any.go:77 (old path via DynamicAny) -- return proto.MessageV1(mt.New().Interface()), nil
provenance: c784e0a7 WithDetails taking protoadapt.MessageV1 (introduced on this branch)

findings.title: LRS invalid-interval error formats stale nil err
findings.why_it_matters: When the management server sends a missing or invalid load_reporting_interval, operators see the warning "invalid load_reporting_interval: <nil>" and lose the reason (nil, overflow, bad nanos). The rewrite throws away the result of CheckValid() and formats `err`. At that point `err` is the earlier stream.Recv() error, which is always nil on this path. Capturing the CheckValid error and formatting it restores the diagnostic the ptypes.Duration version produced.
findings.suggested_fix: `if err := rInterval.CheckValid(); err != nil { return nil, 0, fmt.Errorf("invalid load_reporting_interval: %v", err) }`
evidence: xds/internal/xdsclient/transport/loadreport.go:174-175 -- if rInterval.CheckValid() != nil { return nil, 0, fmt.Errorf("invalid load_reporting_interval: %v", err)
xds/internal/xdsclient/transport/loadreport.go:165-167 -- resp, err := stream.Recv(); if err != nil { return ... }  (err is nil when line 175 is reached)

residual_risks: Duration conversions in balancer/rls/config.go (convertDuration) and xds LRS now use CheckValid()+AsDuration(). ptypes.Duration rejected values that overflow time.Duration (beyond roughly 292 years). Those values now pass CheckValid (limit is 10000 years) and AsDuration silently clamps them, so such configs are accepted instead of rejected. Low practical impact, but it is a behavior change.

callsite completeness: grep-only. Other exported surfaces whose parameter type changed from APIv1 proto.Message to v2 (internal/testutils.MarshalAny, xDS httpfilter/clusterspecifier interfaces) are internal. They compile under go vet for the reviewed packages, but external consumers were not checked.
testing_gaps: No test runs the default proto codec or status WithDetails/Details round-trip with an APIv1-only (legacy, no ProtoReflect) message type. That test would catch both the codec rejection and the Details unwrap regression.
